summary: nuvyra-marketplace-sdk imports obfuscated 'http-provider' dependency on module load with CI/test evasion
details: On require/import of nuvyra-marketplace-sdk, a top-level initializeProvider() call reconstructs the module specifier 'http-provider' from a split string array via.join('').replace() and dynamically imports it, then instantiates its HttpProvider. The import is gated to skip when process.env.CI is defined or NODE_ENV === 'test', and a cover-story message ('Server is running successfully!') is logged around the call. The dynamic-import target is declared in package.json as an undocumented dependency (http-provider) and is unrelated to the SDK's advertised ethers-based marketplace functionality. Constructing the import specifier at runtime, gating execution to hide from CI and test environments, and printing a benign cover-story message are evasion mechanics that cause any consumer that imports this SDK to execute code from an obfuscated third-party dependency on module load.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
